capabilities: Sync vault files with 12 cloud providers (S3, WebDAV, Dropbox, OneDrive, Google Drive and more)
Resolve conflicts with a 3-way merge engine and timestamped conflict copies
Encrypt synced data with AES-256 or rclone-crypt before it leaves the device
Schedule timed background sync and sync-on-save
Import existing Remotely Save credentials and settings on first launch
extras: Not in the Obsidian community directory; installation is via BRAT or manual download, and the manifest notes the plugin has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian. Known limitations cover large-file transfers on mobile and symlinks, which should be excluded via ignore patterns.
intentEvidence: BYOC is a community-maintained fork of the excellent Remotely Save plugin.
motivation: The maintainers forked Remotely Save to provide a clean, completely self-hosted experience while keeping its robust sync engine.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to sync a vault through the user's own cloud storage, and the original Remotely Save plugin is no longer the focus of this fork's self-hosted direction.

relations.evidence: BYOC is a fork of Remotely Save, originally created by fyears.

requires.name: cloud provider account (Dropbox, OneDrive, Google Drive, Box, Yandex Disk, Kor)
S3 access keys or Azure Blob SAS URL
self-hosted WebDAV/S3 server (Nextcloud, ownCloud, Synology, MinIO)

summary: Self-hosted vault synchronization plugin, forked from Remotely Save, that syncs notes to 12 cloud providers with encryption and conflict handling.
